children: Turkish consumer price inflation climbed to 2.58% month-on-month in October, above expectations and driven by clothing and food price rises, while the annual figure was 29.77%, data from the Turkish Statistical Institute showed on Tuesday.
Clothing and footwear prices surged 12.58% during the month, while food prices rose 3.5% and transport prices were up 2.02%.

In a Reuters poll, monthly consumer price inflation was forecast to be 2.4%, driven by higher energy price pressures as well as seasonally higher clothing and food prices, and the annual rate was seen at 29.56%.
In September, consumer prices rose 1.84% month-on-month and 29.73% year-on-year, below forecasts.

The poll's median estimate sees annual inflation at 29.57% by the end of 2026.
Turkey's central bank kept its year-end interim inflation target at 24% while raising its year-end inflation forecast to 28% in its third inflation report published in August.

Last Friday, the central bank said higher energy and commodity prices driven by geopolitical tensions continued to pose upside risks to inflation, a week after it cut its policy rate by 100 basis points to 36% at its October 22 meeting, its first cut since January.
Tuesday's data also showed the domestic producer price index rose 1.65% month-on-month in October for an annual increase of 27.41%.
